boundary_rationale: The maskil-le-Ethan title heads the psalm (מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל לְאֵיתָ֥ן הָֽאֶזְרָחִֽי, web:Ps.89.0 = oshb:Ps.89.1) and the opening verse states the composition’s own double topic — “I will sing of the loving kindness of Yahweh forever” (web:Ps.89.1) — before the psalmist’s declaration turns, at 89:3, into a quoted first-person divine oath: “I have made a covenant with my chosen one, I have sworn to David, my servant” (web:Ps.89.3). The unit closes on that oath’s own guarantee, “I will establish your offspring forever, and build up your throne to all generations” (web:Ps.89.4), corroborated by Selah (web:Ps.89.4 = oshb:Ps.89.5).
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading closes the unit at web:Ps.89.2 (oshb:Ps.89.3) and opens the next at web:Ps.89.3 (oshb:Ps.89.4), where oshb:Ps.89.3 closes in the psalmist's own second-person address to Yahweh, תָּכִ֖ן אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ בָהֶֽם, and oshb:Ps.89.4 opens in Yahweh's own first-person oath, כָּרַ֣תִּֽי בְ֭רִית לִבְחִירִ֑י — a genuine speaker shift this candidate discloses rather than resolves. Selah at web:Ps.89.4 (oshb:Ps.89.5) corroborates a close there only as tier-3 evidence, not as the ground for holding the oath inside this unit.
observed_substrate_signals: superscription genre label maskil + attribution le-Ethan opens the psalm (tier-1)
first-person vow (89:1-2) shifts into quoted divine oath at 89:3 with no intervening topic marker
Selah closes the unit at web:Ps.89.4 = oshb:Ps.89.5 (tier-3 corroboration)
device_notes: Psalm 89 is a single composition; every row here shares one parent, Psalm 89, from title to closing doxology. Selah corroborates this unit’s close (web:Ps.89.4 = oshb:Ps.89.5).

boundary_rationale: The psalm opens in third-person description, “He who dwells…” (web:Ps.91.1), before the voice turns to first-person confession, “I will say of…” (web:Ps.91.2). The second-person address that opens at web:Ps.91.3 (יַ֭צִּֽילְךָ, oshb:Ps.91.3) has not yet begun, so the third-person description and its first-person confession stand together as one unit before the address begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: web:Ps.91.3 shifts both grammatical person and addressee, opening the protective second-person address that governs the rest of the psalm rather than continuing the speaker's own confession, so folding it into this row was rejected.
observed_substrate_signals: oshb:Ps.91.1's opening participle יֹ֭שֵׁב (oshb:Ps.91.1, 'dwells') names a generic figure, not an addressed 'you'

the person chain moves from the 3ms participle יֹ֭שֵׁב (oshb:Ps.91.1) to the 1cs forms אֹמַ֗ר and אֶבְטַח (oshb:Ps.91.2) to the 2ms-suffixed יַ֭צִּֽילְךָ (oshb:Ps.91.3), where the second-person address begins
device_notes: Rows of Psalm 91 group to one parent unit.

boundary_rationale: oshb:Ps.91.13 closes on the second-person address תִּרְמֹ֖ס כְּפִ֣יר וְתַנִּֽין (oshb:Ps.91.13), and web:Ps.91.14 opens with the causal clause כִּ֤י בִ֣י חָ֭שַׁק וַאֲפַלְּטֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.14, 'because he has clung to me and I will deliver him'), a first-person divine verb shifting the speaker from the second-person address-voice of oshb:Ps.91.3-Ps.91.13 to Yahweh's own voice, sustained by אֲ֝שַׂגְּבֵ֗הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.14), וְֽאֶעֱנֵ֗הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.15) and אַשְׂבִּיעֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.16). This closing oracle, in which God speaks of the trusting individual in the third person ('him'), is a distinct unit from the second-person address that precedes it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating web:Ps.91.13 as the oracle's opening verse was rejected because it still addresses 'you' in the second person, while web:Ps.91.14 is where Yahweh's own first-person voice begins.
observed_substrate_signals: the 1cs divine verb וַאֲפַלְּטֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.14) opens the shift against the 2ms address of oshb:Ps.91.3-Ps.91.13, with the psalm's other 1cs verbs disclosed at oshb:Ps.91.2 (אֹמַ֗ר, אֶבְטַח)

the verb וַאֲפַלְּטֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Ps.91.14, 'and I will deliver him') is first-person, first-person divine speech -- Yahweh's own voice, distinct in speaker from the third-person and second-person address of the rest of the psalm, though not the psalm's only first-person verb -- 2 occurrences (אֹמַ֗ר/אֶבְטַח) recur at oshb:Ps.91.2, also 1cs
device_notes: The closing oracle carries the psalm's direct divine first-person speech, distinct in voice from its other three spans.

boundary_rationale: A new wayyiqtol verb introduces a new named subject: “Israel also came into Egypt” (web:Ps.105.23) — MT reads 'וַיָּבֹ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מִצְרָ֑יִם' (oshb:Ps.105.23) — turning from Joseph individually to Israel corporately. “He increased his people greatly” (web:Ps.105.24) and “turned their heart to hate his people” (web:Ps.105.25) set up the oppression that “He sent Moses, his servant, and Aaron” answers (web:Ps.105.26), the Hebrew 'שָׁ֭לַח מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדּ֑וֹ' at oshb:Ps.105.26; the unit closes with Moses and Aaron performing “miracles among them, and wonders in the land of Ham” (web:Ps.105.27), the general statement the plague catalogue itemizes from 105:28.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through the whole nine-verse plague list was considered, but 105:28 opens the itemized catalogue proper with its own perfect verb ('שָׁ֣לַֽח', roughly 'he sent [darkness],' oshb:Ps.105.28 — a ketiv/qere note sits later in this verse per pmarks_Ps.json kq, not quoted here), where 105:27 still speaks in the general terms (“miracles… wonders”, web:Ps.105.27) that the catalogue then specifies.
observed_substrate_signals: new wayyiqtol verb with new named subject Israel opens the unit (105:23), narrative-subject shift from Joseph
unit runs population growth → oppression → the sending of Moses/Aaron → a general miracles/wonders statement that the following catalogue itemizes
device_notes: The plague sequence itemized from 105:28-36 names 9 distinct plague nouns in the psalm's own bytes: darkness (חֹ֭שֶׁךְ, 105:28), blood (לְדָ֑ם, 105:29), frogs (צְפַרְדְּעִ֑ים, 105:30), swarming things and lice (עָרֹ֑ב and כִּ֝נִּ֗ים, 105:31), hail (בָּרָ֑ד, 105:32), locusts and young locusts (אַרְבֶּ֑ה and וְ֝יֶ֗לֶק, 105:34), and the firstborn (בְּכ֣וֹר, 105:36); a cross-book relation to Exodus's narrative noted as texture, not boundary authority for these rows.

boundary_rationale: The row opens at web:Ps.109.6 where an unmarked singular “him” replaces the plural accusers of the preceding row—הַפְקֵ֣ד עָלָ֣יו רָשָׁ֑ע (web:Ps.109.6 = oshb:Ps.109.6, “Set a wicked man over him”)—and no reported-speech verb (a 'saying' or 'who say' construction) introduces the shift; on the frame bytes this reads as the psalmist continuing his own prayer against a singular, representative adversary rather than resuming a quotation of the accusers’ own words. A jussive curse-chain runs unbroken through the span, opening יִֽהְיֽוּ (oshb:Ps.109.8) and carrying an interior fatherless-root echo: בָנָ֥יו יְתוֹמִ֑ים (web:Ps.109.9 = oshb:Ps.109.9, “his children be fatherless”) and, echoing it, ח֝וֹנֵ֗ן לִיתוֹמָֽיו (web:Ps.109.12 = oshb:Ps.109.12, “no one to extend kindness...to have pity on his fatherless children”)—two distinct fatherless-root spellings, swept separately: 109:9's spelling recurs in 3 verses book-wide (2 outside this span); 109:12's spelling is unique to 109:12 book-wide (1 verse), inside this span. The unit closes on יְהִֽי אַחֲרִית֥וֹ לְהַכְרִ֑ית (web:Ps.109.13 = oshb:Ps.109.13, “Let his posterity be cut off”).
strongest_rejected_alternative: A minority reading takes web:Ps.109.6-Ps.109.19 as the psalmist quoting the very curse his accusers pronounced against him—resuming, after the intervening description, the reported speech flagged by web:Ps.109.2’s “They have spoken to me with a lying tongue” so that the singular “him” is the psalmist himself. The Hebrew supplies no quotation-opening verb at the web:Ps.109.5|Ps.109.6 seam to settle the question, so this rival is a live, byte-honest alternative, not excluded by the frame.
observed_substrate_signals: referent narrows to singular עָלָ֣יו at oshb:Ps.109.6 with no reported-speech verb introducing it
jussive verb forms (יִֽהְיֽוּ oshb:Ps.109.8, אַל יְהִי oshb:Ps.109.12) run through the span

fatherless-root forms at oshb:Ps.109.9 and oshb:Ps.109.12 are two distinct spellings, swept separately: 109:9's spelling = 3 verses book-wide (2 outside this span); 109:12's spelling = 1 verse book-wide (109.12 only, inside this span)
device_notes: The jussive curse-chain opening here is the psalm's most-debated internal seam; its imprecatory register continues into web:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.20 under the same jussive grammar apart from the motive particle יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר at oshb:Ps.109.16 alone, whose clause runs through the wayyiqtols of oshb:Ps.109.17-18 (וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב, וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ) before the jussive resumes at oshb:Ps.109.19 (תְּהִי), the kinship reversal to אֲ֭בֹתָיו (oshb:Ps.109.14) marking the turn.

boundary_rationale: An acclamation naming Yahweh's own act, “The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous” (web:Ps.118.15), doubles its own closing clause (יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל (oshb:Ps.118.15), “The right hand of Yahweh does valiantly”) at web:Ps.118.16, byte-identical (collate.py, byte tier, 2 verses); the strophe then turns to the speaker's own voice, marked by the first-person forms אָמ֥וּת, אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה and וַ֝אֲסַפֵּ֗ר at oshb:Ps.118.17 (absent from oshb:Ps.118.15-Ps.118.16), “I will not die, but live, and declare Yah's works” (web:Ps.118.17), and its cost, “Yah has punished me severely, but he has not given me over to death” (web:Ps.118.18).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the row at v16 (doubled right-hand refrain alone) would cut the acclamation off from the survival declaration it grounds: the 1cs forms of oshb:Ps.118.17 (אָמ֥וּת, אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה, וַ֝אֲסַפֵּ֗ר) are absent from oshb:Ps.118.15-Ps.118.16, so v17 answers in the speaker's own voice what this candidate reads as vv15-16's communal acclamation.
observed_substrate_signals: web:Ps.118.15's closing clause (יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל (oshb:Ps.118.15)) is byte-identical (2 verses) to web:Ps.118.16's closing clause

oshb:Ps.118.15 and oshb:Ps.118.16 carry no first-person form at all, distinct from the first-person testimony of oshb:Ps.118.17-18 (אָמ֥וּת, אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה, וַ֝אֲסַפֵּ֗ר at 118:17; יִסְּרַ֣נִּי, נְתָנָֽנִי at 118:18); WEB brackets יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל in its own quotation marks across web:Ps.118.15-16, translation punctuation that is tier-4 and carries no evidentiary weight here.
device_notes: The doubled right-hand-of-Yahweh acclamation (vv15-16) carries no first-person form; the speaker's own survival testimony (vv17-18) answers it with the first-person forms of oshb:Ps.118.17-18 (אָמ֥וּת, אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה, וַ֝אֲסַפֵּ֗ר, יִסְּרַ֣נִּי, נְתָנָֽנִי).

boundary_rationale: Three interpretive declarations follow the preceding scene: אֶ֭בֶן מָאֲס֣וּ הַבּוֹנִ֑ים הָ֝יְתָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ פִּנָּֽה (oshb:Ps.118.22) (“The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.” web:Ps.118.22), “This is Yahweh's doing. It is marvelous in our eyes” (web:Ps.118.23 = oshb:Ps.118.23, whose Hebrew demonstrative זֹּ֑את sits at word index 3, not the verse-initial position its English rendering suggests), together with “This is the day that Yahweh has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!” (web:Ps.118.24 = oshb:Ps.118.24, the row's only genuinely verse-initial demonstrative, זֶה) -- a triad of interpretive sayings rather than the antiphonal request-and-reply shape of the gate scene at 118:19-21. The verse-initial demonstrative device itself is not what unites the triad -- within Psalm 118 the verse-initial demonstrative stands at 118:20 and 118:24 only (2 verses), so it actually straddles this row's own opening seam at 118:21|118:22 (118:20 sits in the preceding row) rather than running through all three of this row's verses. The triad's own unity rests on its shared interpretive-declaration shape and its position after the gate liturgy, not on a verse-initial demonstrative.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching the rejected-stone saying (v22) to the gate scene that precedes it is possible on liturgical-procession grounds, but v22 introduces a fresh image (building, not gate) interpreted by the This-is sayings of vv23-24 rather than continuing the gate dialogue.
observed_substrate_signals: of web:Ps.118.22-24, only v24 opens with a genuine demonstrative (זֶה הַ֭יּוֹם, oshb:Ps.118.24, naming the festal day); v23's demonstrative זֹּ֑את (oshb:Ps.118.23) names the stone's reversal but sits at word index 3, after the opening prepositional phrase מֵאֵ֣ת יְ֭הוָה ('from Yahweh'); v22 has no demonstrative at all

the rejected-stone saying's original setting (building metaphor, royal or communal) is not settled by the row's own bytes; the referent of 'the stone' is an open interpretive question this candidate holds rather than resolves
device_notes: The This-is triad (vv22-24) interprets the reversal just enacted, sitting between the gate liturgy (vv19-21) and the festal procession (vv25-27).

boundary_rationale: A final personal declaration -- אֵלִ֣י אַתָּ֣ה וְאוֹדֶ֑ךָּ ("my God, you, and I will thank you") and אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אֲרוֹמְמֶֽךָּ ("my God, I will exalt you") (oshb:Ps.118.28, web:Ps.118.28 “You are my God, and I will give thanks to you. You are my God, I will exalt you.”) -- names God with two distinct Hebrew words (אֵלִ֣י, אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י) that WEB renders identically as "You are my God," the doubling a rendering effect rather than a repeated Hebrew lexeme -- closes the psalm with its opening line repeated verbatim: הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.118.29) is byte-identical (collate.py, byte tier) to הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.118.1), a true hodu inclusio framing all 29 verses of the psalm.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v29 as belonging with the altar procession at 118:25-27 would merge the closing inclusio into festal-procession texture; the word-for-word repetition of v1 (7 words) instead marks v29 as the psalm's deliberate frame-closing verse.
observed_substrate_signals: web:Ps.118.29 (הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.118.29)) is byte-identical (2 verses) to web:Ps.118.1 (הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.118.1)) across their shared 7-word formula

web:Ps.118.28 names God with two distinct 1cs-suffixed forms in one verse, אֵלִ֣י ('my God/El') and אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י ('my God/Elohim') (oshb:Ps.118.28) -- WEB's identical 'You are my God' rendering of both is a translation effect, not a repeated Hebrew word; the verb-plus-2ms-suffix thanksgiving formula this verse shares with oshb:Ps.118.21 (א֭וֹדְךָ, 'I will give thanks to you') is not unique to v28 -- its skeleton sweeps to 14 verses book-wide (12 word-bound), and at byte tier the pointed form stands in 3 verses, oshb:Ps.35.18, oshb:Ps.118.21 and oshb:Ps.119.7
device_notes: This row closes the hodu inclusio opened at web:Ps.118.1-4, the psalm's outermost frame.
